utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom, and welcome again to all of you back from what I suppose should have been a very productive but also restful break. I hope we are all ready to get moving and get a very smooth ride, having got that length of a break. Mr. Court Officer, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances, please, for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. Welcome back to The Hague, and a happy new year to Your Honours. Counsel, the same to you. Mark Harmon, Barney Thomas, Dan Saxon, and Carmela Javier appearing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Welcome to the warm and sunny Hague. Boris Zorko, I would like to introduce to you as our new case manager; he's been around these halls before. Mr. Mair -- Chad Mair, Tina Drolec, and we have with us today two of our interns to sit in, and Mr. Alex Fielding, and Orla Cronin. I'm Gregor Guy-Smith, and Mr. Novak Lukic and I are representing Mr. Perisic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and welcome back to you also, Mr. Perisic. Just before we start with the proceedings of the day, can we do a few housekeeping matters, please, two oral decisions that the Chamber would like to render. On the 18th of January, 2010, the Prosecution filed its confidential request for change in status of certain exhibits -- I beg your pardon. May the Chamber please move into private session. I'm sorry; it's the fact of the holiday.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. On the 18th of January, 2010, the Prosecution filed its second Prosecution filing pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision of the 21st of December, 2009, regarding the outstanding documents marked for identification whereby the Prosecution requests the admission into evidence of six documents; namely, P1279, P1371, P1809, P2149, P2150, and P2151, previously marked for identification. The decision of the 21st of December, 2009, denied the admission into evidence of these documents without prejudice until such time as a number of conditions set out therein were met. The Prosecution now submits that such conditions have been complied with. Once again, does the Defence have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. With the understanding that the Prosecution has complied with this Court's orders, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Well, the Trial Chamber is then satisfied that the conditions as set out in its decision on the 21st of December have been met, admits the mentioned documents into evidence, and orders the following: 1. In relation to P1279, the corresponding B/C/S and English transcripts shall be attached to this exhibit. 2. In relation to P1371, the revised B/C/S translation shall replace the one currently on e-court. 3. In relation to P1809, the full English translation shall replace the six partial and incomplete ones currently on e-court. 4. In relation to P1249, P1250, P1251, for each of these three exhibits the Prosecution shall re-upload on e-court the B/C/S document completed with the prior-to missing page so that each shall form one complete item. I wish to beg your pardon. I have a problem. I realise that that last paragraph 4 refers to 1249, 1250, 1251. The first paragraphs refer to 2149, 2150 -- and 2150. I beg to withdraw this decision. It will be re-rendered. Thank you. Having done that, may I call Mr. Harmon, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have one remaining witness to call, and that is Mr. Garry Selsky this morning. We will not be recalling Mr. Randall. I communicated to the Trial Chamber and to Defence counsel the status of P600, which is a photograph that purported to come from the Orahovac site. That is not the photograph of the ammunition box that was recovered at the Orahovac site. It was recovered at another site. Therefore, we will not recall Mr. Randall. We will limit our evidence today to Mr. Garry Selsky. Apologies to the Court for any inconvenience that it occasioned by virtue of our submission. Same to the Defence. Mr. Thomas will lead the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Am I right to say the next witness is 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Before I call Mr. Selsky, who I don't intend to examine, being a 92 bis witness, but he's required to attend for cross-examination, Your Honours, I wonder if I could just deal firstly with his -- first of all, the declaration which Your Honours have already ruled is to be admitted as an exhibit. The relevant P number was 1833. It was -- Your Honours ruled that it was to be admitted as an exhibit following redaction of certain portions. Those redactions have now been undertaken, and the redacted declaration has been up-loaded into e-court. I don't know if anything by way of any formal tendering of that particular document as an exhibit is required, given Your Honours' ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Court Officer is trying to update me. I'm not quite sure I'm on the same page as you are, Mr. Thomas. All I know is that you've asked for Mr. Selsky to come and testify. What exhibit he's coming to testify on, I really don't know. However, Mr. Court Officer seems to be on the same page as you, and he wants to give us an explanation which is very complicated for me as to what has happened so far with respect to the e-court position of that exhibit. Mr. Court Officer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to simplify my explanation. The document under 65 ter number 08234, which was redacted and up-loaded into e-court under 65 ter 08234A, has been assigned Exhibit P1833 and has been admitted into evidence, though it still lacks redacted B/C/S translation to be attached to it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: But it's still in evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If I might, just for a minor point of clarification. With regard to this Court's ruling concerning this particular document, paragraph G of the document, it is our position, continues to contain opinions and references to unnamed parties which the Prosecution, in their initial submission, indicated they would strike from this declaration. So to that extent, we believe that it would still be appropriate that paragraph G be stricken, even in light of the ruling made by this Court, because it falls within the legal understanding and the undertaking made by the Prosecution as it relates to any opinions or references made to unnamed third parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that may have been the position of the parties, but it was not ultimately the position of Your Honours. And in your decision, you stated very clearly which parts of the declaration were to remain and which were to be redacted. So it was purely conforming with the very specific directions contained in Your Honours' decision that the present exhibit was redacted in the way that it was. The Prosecution simply isn't at liberties to do otherwise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As I said earlier, we don't have the exhibit before us, and we're not here dealing with admissions of exhibits, if a decision has been taken to admit a particular exhibit, it has been admitted. If anybody wants to challenge that admission, we can do that at a separate stage. At this point in time, we're really trying to get the witness into court.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, one matter before Mr. Selsky comes in. In preparing for his evidence today, he went back through the analysis that he had undertaken. In the course of doing so, he found a number of errors which he has corrected by way of a further declaration over the weekend that was taken in accordance with 92 bis before a Registry officer yesterday. That also has been up-loaded into e-court and provided to the Defence. It does no more than identify what corrections he wishes to make to the numbers that are recorded in his original declaration. And for the purpose of having the complete picture, Your Honours, I'm seeking at this moment to tender also as an exhibit the supplemental 92 bis declaration that Mr. Selsky swore yesterday. That document has been up-loaded into e-court. We can put it on the screens, if that will assist Your Honours. But I see my learned friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. In the spirit of the new year, considering the state of this particular witness's testimony, we will have no objection to the Prosecution's proposed correction of the previous 92 bis declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to my learned friend for that indication, Your Honours. The 65 ter number concerned is 08234B, and if that could please be tendered as an exhibit, if Your Honours so agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, it may be tendered. Okay. 65 ter 08234B is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2892. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. Registrar, that concludes all preliminary matters relating to Mr. Selsky. He can be called for cross-examination at this point, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He may come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the oath, standing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Selsky. Before you sit down, what does P stand for, Mr. Selsky, in your initials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paul.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Mr. Thomas. Sorry, your learned friend is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was being a bit eager, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. I thought you were not able to drink water seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll have to try and see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, could you give us your full name and occupation, please.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: My name is Garry Paul Selsky. I'm a member of the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm a senior investigator, and have been since September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you're the author of a declaration dated October 2007 and also the supplementary declaration dated yesterday that have been tendered in support of account of Srebrenica-related shell casings?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: October 2007, yes, and yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Selsky, would you please answer any questions that my learned friends may have for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Selsky.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Happy new year to you.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: As well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated that you've been an investigator since 1998, and, as I understood it, a senior investigator as well. I take it that's since that time as well, since 1998?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. I have been an investigator since 1972 in my home jurisdiction of Canada, and I commenced here in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to your investigation as a -- in Canada, domestically, what kind of investigations did you do, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Everything from murder, sexual assault, to organised crime, drugs, immigration and passport. In municipal jurisdictions, from battery thefts to different complaints of family abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say, so we don't have to detail your career, that you are certainly a well seasoned and well qualified investigator; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in that regard, in terms of your seasoning and qualifications, you understand both the methodology of investigations and the importance of maintaining particular types of chronologies or, let's say, sheets that indicate the manner in which the investigation's gone forth; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also, of course, understand, as a seasoned and experienced investigator, the importance of memorialising all of the contacts that you have made and the individuals that you have dealt with in your investigation; true?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I didn't catch the word, "context "or "contacts"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Contacts. Individuals who you have dealt with in your investigation. True?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the reason for that being important, and by that I'm talking about is the memorialisation of what I would call time, place, and individual, is so that there is a clear understanding of what you've done in your investigation as well as a chain of evidence, correct, among others?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Chain of evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Chain of evidence, so that we know where the evidence was found and where the evidence -- and how the evidence came to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On evidence seizures made in the field or here, we would bring it -- complete a MIF, describe the items --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't mean to interrupt you. I'm talking just about generally the issue of the importance of memorialising all of the participants and the dates in which things occurred. That's all I'm talking about for the moment.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's something that's pretty important, is it not?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as an investigation becomes larger and there is more evidence to seize or more evidence to investigate, that issue also exponentially becomes something of greater importance because of the need to make sure that the items seized are properly identified; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to take -- I think you mentioned an MIF, seizures went through MIF.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to take a -- you mentioned, I think it was MIF; seizures went through MIF?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, I'm not familiar with that particular acronym. I don't know whether the Chamber is. Could you please explain to us what MIF is?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Just off the top of my head, it's just a procedure in regards -- electronic procedure in how we register evidence into the evidence room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And what does MIF stand for?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I just -- I don't have a recollection right now. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to your efforts in this regard, and by that I'm talking about your efforts with regard to the question of the -- as I understand it, the identification of small-arms cartridges, what I'd like to do for a moment is understand something. And do you, by any chance -- if we could have P1833, which I believe is the declaration that you have submitted in this regard, up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you can stop there for the moment, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone. Would the speakers kindly pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have the interpreter? If you put on your earphones, she's asking you: One, to speak into the microphone, and also that the parties, I think both of you, speak loudly and speak into the microphone. I can't see what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All right. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To pause between questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To pause between questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before we discuss your declaration specifically: Did you keep a chronology of the documents that you reviewed with regard to your efforts to determine the provenance or the identity of small cartridge casings?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I started with the Dean Manning investigations report and his findings on Srebrenica, and I worked down from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it you have a document that reflects all of the times that you have reviewed, signed OTP statements. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have a document that indicates the chronological efforts you made with regard to review of all the documents you reviewed in preparation of this particular declaration; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you rephrase that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have a document, the same kind of thing, a chronology?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And with regard to the OTP investigators that you have spoken to during 2003/2007, I take it once again, based upon your previous two answers, that you have no document that reflects your chronology of speaking with various OTP investigators as it relates to this particular issue. And once again I'm talking about the issue of small-arms cartridges.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could have your declaration up on the screen now. I believe that we've just dealt with -- first of all, looking at this, and perhaps we should look at the first page, and I do apologise. I want to make sure this is the declaration that you take as being your own, that you signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interpose on that point. I see that the declaration on the screen has some redactions on it. I have and I believe the rest of the Chamber has been provided with a hard copy which is unredacted. My question, really, is: What do we go by? Do we go by what's P1833 that's redacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, and I will be questioning about P1833 as redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could take a look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at this to see what has been admitted as P1833 is, in fact, the declaration that you read and signed. Do you recall, on the 26th of November, 2009, being in the presence of the Registrar with Mr. Harmon and signing a declaration?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at the next page, it says: "Declaration by a Person Making a Written Statement Pursuant to Rule 92 Bis." Do you recall being present when this document was executed?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that is your signature where it says "Witness's Signature"; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: At the bottom, yes, left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You will note on the next page there are a number of areas that have now been blackened or redacted, and I trust that as you look at the document, you'll be able to make a determination whether or not this is the declaration that you did, indeed, execute. And looking at the first page, do you recall this language?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we go to the second page just to make sure that that's your signature, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think we've gone the wrong way. I think we need to go the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at the bottom of that page, is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excellent. And now if we could return to the first page of the declaration, itself, which should be back one page. And if we could focus on paragraph 3(A). As I understand what you actually did here, was it you retrieved 3.638 small-arms cartridges or shell casings in the OTP evidence vault; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to that statement, just going that far, no further, when did you do that?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: At the end of August 2007 and throughout the first two weeks of September 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to that particular activity, I take it that the evidence vault is a place that you do not have free access to, but, rather, it's a place where you have to sign -- you have to sign for the actual evidence to take it out so there's a record of what's been in the evidence vault and what's been taken out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Is there a record or sheet of some sort that indicates when you visited the evidence vault for purposes of engaging in this particular exercise, so that if we were to look, we would see a document that establishes the time that you said that you were there in August, that you came in on a certain date?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I don't know of such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You didn't sign such a document?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you could go into the evidence vault whenever you wanted to; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No. I had to make contact with Susan Artega. She had the keys to the vault. She had the keys to different areas. And she retrieved the items off the exhibit shelves, she removed the bags to a table or a cart area that we used, and she took the exhibits back to those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could you give us just an example -- since from what I understand you can't give us a date specific, could you give us an example of how this process worked? Did you call her up on the phone and say, Hello, Ms. Artega, I'm coming by today and I would like to see the following evidence?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, we had -- I had given her a list of ERN numbers in regards to the shell casings and asked her if she could make a list of those. Subsequently, I would call her and make arrangements to meet on the third floor of the Office of the Prosecutor, and she would either be there or I would meet her at the vault door. And we would go into a portion of the vault area that is used for examination purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And when you got into the portion of the vault area that is used for examination purposes, once again I take it, because I'm not sure as to what occurred, but I take it what happened was that she had brought with her a number of sealed envelopes that contained the actual physical evidence that you were going to examine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The exhibits were in boxes, in bags, five, six metres from where we were working. So she would go to that location, retrieve a box or a bag of cartridge casings, and give it to us, and we would identify it via the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that the only thing that you have not responded to is the issue of the evidence -- the actual physical evidence being sealed, that it came to you in a sealed fashion, so that when you obtained it, it was in a pristine position. By that, I mean that it wasn't open and available for rummaging about? It's a question, sir.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was it sealed? When you got the evidence, was it sealed, in a sealed box, bag, container?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Some of the boxes I observed her breaking a seal. Some of the boxes were opened. Some of the large plastic bags that she took from the shelves were sealed, and some of the bags were unsealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt a little bit, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, at page 18 on your screen, line 6, you say: "... and give it to us." Now, this is, I think, Ms. Artega who would give it to "us." Whom were the "us"? With whom were you in the vault room?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, just the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is: Did you ever have him vetted, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in 2007, when you indicated you retrieved 3.638 small-arms cartridges or shell casings, could you tell me, how did you count them? And I mean, by that, did you have a computer or some form of manner of counting these shell casings? You do it by hand and go one, two, three, four, five?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: And Susan Artega was within eyesight of us and participating in some of the counts, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed that.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Excuse me. In some of the counts, she was right there. Other times, she was walking -- or at a small table near us, or walking to the shelf area to get another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And now I take it that those working notes, and by that I mean simply the pieces of -- let me ask you this: Did you do this on a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Memorialise the number of shell casings?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you retained that piece of paper, I take it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have that piece of paper today?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But you do have it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With a date on it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I don't believe there's a date on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh. And after you -- after you counted up the shell cartridges, you came up with this total number, is that correct, of 3.638?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to continue. You said that, with the same paragraph, which is paragraph 3(A), that they were seized by OTP staff between 1996 and 2001. Now, did you personally seize any of these items of evidence?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The first time that you came in contact with these items of evidence was in August of 2007, when you engaged in your counting?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No. I had completed an examination of some of the same exhibits in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, okay. When you say "some of the same exhibits," I take it there's some document that you have in your possession that shows the correlation between that which you exhibited in 2004 and that which you exhibited in 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I don't have the exact correlation, but there's two documents that I have: One that was completed in November 23rd of 2004 and this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the one that was completed in November 2004, is that a -- is that a document for which you also wrote a declaration? I'm sorry. Are the efforts that you engaged in in 2004 ultimately memorialised in a declaration?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And was that a declaration that was also done for purposes of investigation of this case?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in 2004, when you engaged in those efforts, that you examined, as I understand it, some of the same items of evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I just did a -- a sampling of different bags in a collection of casings that came from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you did "a sampling of different bags ... of casings that came from Srebrenica in 2004," could you -- did you memorialise what bags you took what shells out of for purposes of this sampling that you engaged in?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And you have those records?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I have a spreadsheet, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For my own edification, Mr. Selsky, when you say you did "a sampling of different bags in a collection of casings that came from Srebrenica," do I understand you to say that you have not looked at each cartridge out of the 3.638, you have not looked at each one of the 3.638 shell cartridges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two inspections varied, Your Honour. The first one in 2004 was a sampling where we looked at specific -- each cartridge from a bag of evidence that was taken from Srebrenica, and it was a random sampling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say it was a sampling and you looked at each cartridge, then you confused me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but there was just copious amounts of cartridges in boxes and bags in the exhibit vault, and we just took a sampling to determine if -- what type of shells, casings, there were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And just so that we understand exactly what you mean by "sampling," my question to you is: Do I understand you to say you did not examine each cartridge of the 3.638? You examined a few out of several bags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in 2004 we took a sampling of our ERN bags, okay. And when we just took this bag and then randomly took another bag, we would look at what was the content of each bag and how many casings there were, and what decriptives they were. So we might go past ERN 8 or A00-01234 and we might take A00-01235 and miss an exhibit bag. In the 2007, we asked for a number of ERN ranges, and when we looked in each bag, we examined each shell individually. And at times we looked at the bottom of the shell with a magnifying-glass because there was corrosion. They came from excavation sites, so there was rusting of some of the cartridges. So when the shell, at the bottom, when it wasn't -- the case markings weren't visible, we would discard that item and we wouldn't -- we wouldn't guess or we wouldn't make any further examination of it. We would just discard it -- or not discard it, but put it to the side with the collection that we had been going through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is your short answer that you did a sampling in 2004, but in 2007 you looked at each one of the 3.638? That's your short answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to your 2004 findings, and I'm now looking at paragraph D of your declaration, if we could scroll down so you can see it, I take it that part of what you were just discussing with His Honour is contained in the very first sentence, in which you said that you tried to determine what factory engraving marks were present and what year they were manufactured. If you couldn't get that information, then you didn't include that in your sampling? Correct? I'm asking if that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. My friend may have simply misspoken or he may be at cross-purposes, and I just wanted to clarify something for the record. He prefaced his question by saying that In relation to your 2004 findings, and then he quoted from the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I meant 2007. I misspoke, and thank you very much, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With Mr. Thomas' correction, let me repeat my question. With respect to your 2007 findings, you looked at each shell casing to determine what factory engraving marks were present and what year were their manufacture. If you found some that you were not able to make that determination, then you took them out of the equation; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, they were still in the count, but they -- they weren't identified as a PPU 1993 or PPU 1994, or as the schedule indicates; it was just another shell that we -- we also didn't count a PPU shell from 1989 or 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure, okay. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just going to say: How many of the shells did you find that were not identifiable by a PPU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't specifically record that information, Your Honour, as it was -- it wasn't in our finding, it was just put aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, the statement "it wasn't in our finding." I'm not sure I understand exactly what you mean by that, so we'll come back to the issue of those that you put aside. But just for purposes of just trying to get at some understanding here of the process that you did engage in: As of November of 2007, you examined 3.638 seized shell casings; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: According to my affidavit or my declaration yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not talking about your declaration yesterday. I'm talking about what you did in 2007. That's what you said you'd done; right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I understand your testimony correctly, that means that you had the opportunity to look at, examine, all of the shell casings that you'd examined in 2004, plus some additional number; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the declaration that you just recently filed, whose number, I believe, is P2892, indicates that there are an additional six shells; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And so between the time that you signed your declaration in 2009 and over the weekend, you determined that you were shy by six shells, correct, six shell casings?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I looked at the MIF, the exhibit report numbers, and in the lines listed, I noticed the discrepancies. And at that time I notified Mr. Thomas of my findings on Friday late afternoon, when I visited the same vault with Susan Artega, the same individual that gave me the exhibits before, and we examined each bag to make sure that that count reflected the same count that the MIF -- the exhibit report had indicated, and I made my corrections thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith. And just to give everybody a forward warning, given the fact that we started 30 minutes late this morning, this session will end at 12.00 so that we go back to our normal times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, continuing with your declaration, paragraph D, that is, you've indicated the shell casings were predominantly manufactured from the Prvi Partizan Uzice, PPU factory, at Uzice, Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Are you referring to paragraph D?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I probably have a problem with English here. When you say "predominantly manufactured from," are you suggesting that they were partially manufactured from that factory and partially from another, but the predominant manufacturing took place at this factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And not talking about numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Following up on the Judge's question, did you make a determination on -- when you used the term "predominantly" here, did you make a determination of what other places the shell casings were manufactured in?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: There was other markings that related to a factory in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see that you're looking at the screen, so I take it you're getting that information from your declaration.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm refreshing my memory from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. But just so we're clear, you don't have an independent memory of this examination process that you went through, and you're relying on your declaration for purposes of refreshing your memory with regard to, now, the specific issue as to where the shell casings, in your estimation, were manufactured; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I have to object, Your Honour. That's a compound question where the first half asserts or suggests that he does not have an independent memory of this examination process, and it ends with "turning to the specific issue as to where the shell casings were manufactured." These are two different things, Your Honours, and I don't want that answer to be interpreted as suggesting that Mr. Selsky doesn't have an independent memory or recollection of this examination process.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate Mr. Thomas' testifying with regard to Mr. Selsky's memory. Mr. Selsky's asked the question, he's clearly a seasoned investigator, and he can answer the question in the manner that he sees fit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you accept that the question was compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, the question is compound. First of all, you have no independent memory; secondly, you are relying on your declaration for purposes of refreshing your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the specific issue of the manufacturing, which is what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's two -- there are two -- more than one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's qualified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can take it a step at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have an independent memory of where the shell casings were manufactured?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: All of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question is: Do you have an independent memory?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with regard to Prvi Partizan Uzice, do you know where -- do you know where that was independently? Did you independently investigate that area? Did you go to the factory?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: And Kasimir Pikos [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: An investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Kasimir Pikos is an investigator?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the Partizan factory, in terms of the analysis that you were engaged in, did you make any determinations with regard to the relationship that the Partizan factory had with the Government of the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you make a determination about any contracts that existed between the Partizan factory and the Government of the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you make any determinations about any contracts for production of ammunition made between the VRS and the Partizan factory?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you examine at any point in time any documents that would establish a financial relationship between either the Republic of Srpska, and by that I mean the government, or the VRS with regard to the issue of the ordering and payment by those entities for ammunition?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the next sentence in your declaration, in D, you say: "There was a small percentage from Igman Konjic," then it says, "YK (UK) factory at Konjic BiH which was taken over by HOS Croatian forces in 17 April 1992." So before we go any further, I take it that those cartridges, in your examination of them, had some kind of markings upon them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know who was using those cartridges, and by that I mean what side of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm unaware.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the -- with regard to the issue of the PPU cartridges, those that you were able to identify as PPU cartridges, were you able to make a determination as to which side of the conflict was using those cartridges, or did you find that cartridges were something rather fungible? And by that I mean that all sides used what was available to them, however they could get their hands upon them?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm unaware.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your conclusion here that there was a small percentage from Igman Konjic is based upon your examination of those cartridges. And by that I mean there was some kind of a grey marking upon them. True?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If we could turn the page and go to the next page. I'm sorry, before we do that -- excuse me, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before we do that, the last indication in D is: "The cartridges with the engraved markings are described as follows:" Correct? And I'm going back to what you said in paragraph D, the last thing you said in paragraph D. And let's pull it back for you so you know I'm not pulling the wool over your eye. Right: "The cartridges with the engraved markings are described as follows:" And then we go on to the next page; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next page. Thank you very much. If you could just go from where it says "I" just to where the first redaction is, I would appreciate it, and enlarge that part for the gentleman. No, up. Wrong part; up. Yes. Down so he can see the whole thing. Have the screen go down a little bit just so we can see a little bit. Perfect. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated, using designations I, II, III, then IV, and V, those cartridges that have engraved markings on them; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've used, for purposes of describing those cartridges that had engraved markings on them, those that are designated I, II, III, IV and V; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, help me here, if you could, please. Where, on this chart, are those cartridges that you were referring to previously, which are the small percentages from Igman Konjic which apparently had the designation of YK upon them; where are those?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: They aren't indicated in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Now, those cartridges were cartridges that were apparently cartridges dated -- having the date of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Is there a reason why those cartridges are not contained in this chart when you indicate, in paragraph D, the following: "The cartridges with the engraved markings are described as follows:" And it is -- from what I understand your answer to be, that you have clearly deleted, redacted, or left out, whatever word you choose to adopt here, sir, cartridges that were from the Igman Konjic factory?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: They didn't fall in the time-frame from 1993, 1994, and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know what that means, They didn't fall within the time-frame 1993, 1994, 1995. These were cartridges that were found at the sites by the investigators; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You earlier said -- and page 25, line 21, I said we'd get back to this. Your language was -- this was in response to a question by

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "I was just going to say," this is the Judge, "how many of the shells did you find were not identifiable by a PPU?" And your answer was: "We didn't specifically record that information, Your Honour, as it was -- it wasn't in our finding. It was just put aside." Now, you then, at a point in time, mentioned that you did not put into your findings any cartridges that may have been identified in 1979 or 1989?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, did you find cartridges of 1979 and 1989?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those were cartridges that were found in the sites that are the subject matter of your declaration, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall. I didn't count the ones that we set aside and that I didn't record in my findings here that dealt with 1993/1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: They were in the count, but they weren't counted specifically as 25 from 1969 and so on throughout the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any discussion with your fellow investigators about the import of the date of the ammunition, what significance the date of a shell casing might have?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The date 1993 to 1995 was related to the indictment period, and that's what specifically we looked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your capacity as a senior investigator here for many years, sir, you're well aware of the fact that substantial amounts of ammunition that pre-dated 1993 was used throughout the region by all sides, were you not?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As an investigator, I take it it's your position, and I'm asking the question sincerely, that that information is not critical to an understanding of what was occurring with regard to any possible responsibility or liability of individuals, in terms of transferring ammunition or other material?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't grasp your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Wouldn't you agree with me, sir, that ammunition that was produced before 1993 is critical to an understanding of the liability or responsibility of those individuals who are charged with, among other things, the delivery of materiel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That calls for an opinion on the part of the witness, who is also not the trier of fact in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a senior investigator, let me rephrase --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who was also not a trier of fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He's -- I believe he's objecting that I'm invading -- I'm asking him to invade the providence of the Chamber, and I'm more than happy to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to you for the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your estimation, was the presence of ammunition that pre-dated the indictment period, in the very sites that were part of your declaration, of any import?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you believe that the absence of ammunition, identified ammunition, pre-1993 -- let me rephrase that. Would you agree with me that your report is incomplete, inasmuch as it fails to identify pre-1993 ammunition that was found at the sites?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was tasked to examine the shell casings and look for the shell casings that were manufactured from the period 1993 to 1995. And that was my task, and I effected it as best I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to that response, I take it that was the same task that you had from the very beginning of this endeavour. That was the same task you had in 2004; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have 1D07-0356 up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Considering your last answer, Mr. Selsky, this is your declaration from 2004. And, first of all, let's take a look at it just to make sure that you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could scroll down. And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could look at the bottom, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And do you confirm that this is the declaration that you executed in 2004?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go back to page 1. And with Mr. Perisic's indulgence, because one of these is now in -- I don't know if we can do this, if we can do a split screen and if we can have up on the screen right next to that his declaration in 2007, which would mean that we would have to have the Serbian off for a moment. Can we do that? That would be P1833.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In paragraph B of your 2004 declaration, you indicate what endeavours you went through, which is similar to paragraph D of your 2007 declaration. As a matter of fact, I think that it would be fair to say that apart from the number of seized items in 2004, the number being 1.579, and in 2007 the number being 3.638, that the language of these two paragraphs is substantially similar, if not identical. One of the places where there's a distinction being that in 2004 you indicated "seized casings" in paragraph B, and in 2007 you indicated "seized shell casings." But apart from that, the language is the same; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the identification of those shell casings that were engraved, there is, I would hazard to say, a marked difference in the information that you presented in 2004 from that which you presented in 2007. And by that I mean looking at the 2004 declaration, under B(i), you have "PPU, 1994, 1993, 1992, and pre-1992"; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That information does not exist in your declaration in 2007; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Some of it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the pre-1993 information, that information has been excised from your declaration in 2007; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the next entry, that being B(ii) in your 2004 declaration, none of that information is contained within your declaration in 2007, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page of the 2007 declaration to the next page, that may be of some help to Mr. Selsky.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to the information contained in your 2004 declaration at B(ii), you indicated to us that you were tasked with the responsibility of looking for, if I'm not mistaken, evidence that covered the indictment period that includes the years 1993 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were tasked with the responsibility of looking for, if I'm not mistaken, evidence that covered the indictment period that included the years 1993 and 1994. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Am I correct that in the following -- that with regard to your declaration in 2004, under B(ii), the years 1994 and 1993 would fall directly within the indictment period and directly within the responsibilities for which you were tasked?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Is that a question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It certainly is.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Can you rephrase it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. Am I correct that with regard to your declaration in 2004, under B(ii), the years 1994 and 1993 would fall directly within the indictment period and directly within the responsibilities for which you were tasked?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on, that information is not contained in your declaration in 2007; right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, and it's my recollection that I don't believe we found any, but I don't know why it wasn't included in that 2007 declaration, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, now you've said two things. Now you've said you don't believe you found any, and you don't know why it wasn't included. When you say that you don't believe you found any, when you made this declaration, you made this declaration, I'm assuming, in good faith and certainly telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth with regard to what you'd done. And since these are engraved markings, they clearly are things that you found, aren't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Which declaration are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall the actual numbers that we noted in regards to (ii) 1994, 1993, 1992, and pre-1992, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Well that's distinct from the statement that you've just made, Mr. Selsky, which is, "And it's my recollection that I don't believe we found any," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on to B(iii) of your 2004 declaration, if I'm not mistaken, the entry of "322 92," "322 92" is not contained in your 2007 declaration; correct? The other two items are.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Can you just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. If you take a look at your declaration, 3(iii), you see the numbers "10 94," which I believe is represented in your 2000 [sic] declaration under (iii) as "10 94." And there's a comment; it says "324 94," which I believe is included in your 2000 [sic] declaration under IV. And the last one, "322 92," has gone missing. It's not in your 2007 declaration, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It's -- no, it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With -- if we could have the next page of 1D07-0356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, what would you like to do with 1D07-0356?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I haven't done anything with it yet. I'm moving to the next page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm moving to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page? That would be on the right-hand side of the screen. The other one. Yeah. If it's of difficulty, I can do this another -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd just like to look at the very first two lines -- just the very first two lines: "Total number of ammunition examined," I'm sorry, and then it says under that pre-1992, "1277;" right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, going to your -- that's good. Now, going to your declaration in 2007, I don't see any indication of the number of pre-1992 ammunition totals. Do you?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the -- with regard to the numbers that you have supplied us with as related to the 2007 declaration, you indicate, out of the total number of shell casings examined of 3.638, you found the following shell casings were from the years as below described, which comes to a total number of 546, if my math is correct, which means there is a balance of some 3100 -- well, a little bit less, actually, 2900-plus shell casings that I am assuming are pre-1992 shell casings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why didn't you put that figure in? Not important?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thank the Chamber's indulgence. I will not be moving 1D07-0356 into evidence, and I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, in response to my question earlier, you said that the words "predominantly manufactured from Prvi Partizan Uzice" meant that it was partly from there and party from another factory. Which other factory contributed to the manufacture of those that were manufactured predominantly by Prvi Partizan?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The one from Bosnia, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was my question?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: What was the proportionality of the totality of the casings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you've misunderstood my question.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said to me -- the word "predominantly" doesn't refer to numbers, it refers to the manufacturer. Now, you say, if I may quote verbatim from the 2007 declaration, you say: "The shell casings were predominantly manufactured from the Prvi Partizan Uzice PPU factory in Uzice, Serbia."

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Then I didn't grasp your question properly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have still not put my question yet.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The first time you asked me that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I asked you, What do you mean by "predominantly"? Do you mean -- the first time I asked you was, Do you mean by the word "predominantly" that the manufacture was done at more than one factory, but the bulk of the manufacturing took place at Prvi. And you said, Yes. And my question now is: What is or what are the other factories which contributed to the manufacture of those shells that were predominantly manufactured by Prvi Partizan Uzice?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I didn't ask -- answer your question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Correctly.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: -- Correctly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You want to correct that?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you understand me to be asking you? You understood me to be saying the majority of shells came from Prvi?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, and that's my finding and my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if by the word "predominantly" you meant the majority, then I've got to go back and ask you the same -- the question slightly differently now in order that we are on the same page.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, that's fine. According to this declaration, what is the total number of the PPU 1993 to PPU 7.9 that you have on page 2? You've got "PPU 1993, 79," "PPU 1994, 299," and then "10 94, 109," and then 38 through 20. What's the sum total of that?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I didn't add it up. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please add it up right now.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: May I have a pen and paper, please. Thank you. 545, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 545. Would 545 be the majority of 3.638?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No, but in total that's what our findings were of all the shells we looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "totality" in context.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Of all the 3.000 somewhat shells we looked at, predominantly the shells came from or had the markings of PPU; with different years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it's 545. We've just added now. It's 545.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, from the years 1993/1994, but there was other years involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, actually I would like to deal -- I will deal with the question of years later, because I've got a problem with that, too, based on your declaration. But for now, when you say the words "predominantly manufactured from," you meant the majority; I do not understand how 545 can be a majority of 3.638. This is what is in your declaration. I can only deal with what's in your declaration.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I'm saying: How does anyone come to say the predominant product came from Prvi Partizan if only 545 came from there out of a total of 3.638?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It was my understanding, when I was referring to the word "predominant," I was dealing with the 3.000 in total, not just the exact finding of, you know, 545, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I think the record will just have to show that we don't understand each other on that one.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I still don't understand your answer. But talking about the years, and I know that you've been asked extensively on the question of years here, pre-1992, pre-1994, the last sentence in your declaration of 2007, on the first page, says that: "Cartridges with the engraved markings ..." But before I get to that, before I ask you that, after dealing with the Prvi Partizan Uzice, you say: "There was a small percentage from Igman Konjic YK (UK) factory." That's from BiH. I guess you determined that by the markings and engravings on those shells, that they came from Igman Konjic.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, and that they were pre-1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, the problem is this next sentence -- this last sentence on this page says: "The cartridges with the engraved markings are described as follows:" The sentence does not say that "cartridges with engraved markings and dating post-1992 are described as follows:" Therefore, there isn't a basis, in the sentence as written, for excluding pre-1993 casings. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is: Why would they have been excluded if there is no such basis for their exclusion in your declaration?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I was tasked with determining if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You haven't told us your task in this document. All you have told us that one of your duties had been to investigate the case against Momcilo Perisic, who was chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia from 1993 to 1998. And you've told us that you were examining casings that were found in the Srebrenica killings of -- I must be sure -- I mustn't use an unredacted document when we have a redacted document. Can we go to the first page of the right-hand side, please? No, that's not it, that's not it. On the left-hand side. The first page of that document that's redacted on the screen, please. Thank you. Okay. On this one, can we enlarge it a little bit, please. Thank you. In trying to determine your task from this declaration, sir, we are referred -- we see that you say here: "I previewed signed OTP statements, documents, and spoke to OTP investigators during that period. I note my findings. I retrieved 3.638 small-arms cartridges or shell casings in the OTP evidence vault that were seized by OTP staff between 1996 and 2001 from execution sites and primary and secondary burial sites in the Srebrenica area, BiH." From that, the only impression I can get is that you're investigating the whole thing that you are talking about there.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I understand your point, Your Honour, and I should have made it much more clear in my declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much if you accept that you should have made it much more clearer in your declaration. Thank you for the explanation. Now, my last question: If you could just take us through your declarations and tell us the significance of the writings that you've got there, you know. And I am assuming that "PPU 1993" means that it comes from the Prvi Partizan Uzice and it was manufactured in 1993. Is that what it means?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: That's my understanding, but I don't have any expertise in that area, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What would then "10 94" mean? If you go to the second page of the left-hand side, for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can answer that. I -- we looked at that portion or that stamp, and I wasn't able to answer that through talking with the investigators, and I relied on our trial team to call in an expert for that type of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And, therefore, you can't say that "10 94" comes from PPU?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Similarly, "324 94" you can't say comes from PPU?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does "PPU 7.9" mean?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It's the 7.9 calibre, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So we don't know what year of manufacture these 20 were -- what is the year of manufacture of these 20?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We cannot say they are post-1992, nor can we say they are pre-1993?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess that clarifies me on those little markings. Any re-examination, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honours, thank you. And if we could please have -- in fact, we may have it on the screen already. If we could have page 1, please -- sorry, the previous page of the declaration that's on the left-hand side of the screen, please. And if we could have paragraph D enlarged, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Selsky, I want to take you back again to the statement of yours that the shell casings were predominantly manufactured at Prvi Partizan. You examined something in excess of three and a half thousand casings?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Of those three and a half thousand casings, was there a marking that most of them bore?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: "PPU."

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Were they just from 1993 or 1994, or were they from other years as well?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: From the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s, and early 1990 markings, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in your declaration, please. In the bottom section of numbers that we've already discussed, the section that adds up to 545, you have included listings for PPU 1993 and 1994. You see that?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You've already given us your explanation as to why you limited your description to 1993 and 1994, but do we take it that there were a significant number of PPU shells that you observed with markings of 1992 or earlier?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, and that's where I derived predominantly from there was a high percentage; 60, 70 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do I understand, then, that if you add that figure to what we have there, the 545, that you get more than half of 3.600 odd?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think your math might be off. Apart from the fact that it's leading, so the record is clear here, I don't know how we get to the "more than half." I just think your math might be off, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You've used the word "predominantly"?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You've explained to us that in using that word you were attempting to convey that more than half of these 3600 shells were manufactured by Prvi Partizan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
