utterances.text: On the page that we see, page 2 of your declaration, you have listed only 1993 and 1994 entries and some selected others from PPU which add up to 545; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, three, at least, of those relate to PPU; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do I understand that what you have excluded from that list is anything that bore the marking of PPU 1992 or earlier?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. When you add what --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't believe that that's an accurate statement of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe it would be accurate to say that he excluded anything that did not have a 1993 or 1994 marking upon it, but whether it would be PPU or otherwise would not be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I don't understand my friend's objection. I'm asking him if that's what he excluded. I'm not quoting any testimony back to him. I'm asking him if that's what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You should be asking him what did he exclude, rather than telling him what it is you think he excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What did you exclude? In relation to PPU, because that's all I'm interested in at the moment, what did you exclude from that list that we see on the screen on the moment?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The pre-1992 shell casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Pre-1992 or pre-1993? In other words, did you exclude 1992 as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's pre-1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us whether any of those pre-1993 shells also had "PPU" on them?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, and I estimate that approximately 60 to 70 per cent of the casings that we examined of the -- that totalled 3600 casings were from -- had the markings "PPU" on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was your examination in 2007 at the request of the Prosecution team?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And were you asked to look for particular things?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. The ammunition that was manufactured by the PPU factory in the indictment 1993 to 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honours. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one question which is occasioned by the question that you asked, but I'm more than happy to wait until you ask first, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me ask first. Taking you back to my questions, Mr. Selsky, would it then be fair to say, according to this declaration, the total number of PPU shell casings that are post-1992 is 378; that is, 545 minus 109, 38, and 20?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it's in -- the totality of the number is of 3.644.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I would like you to please listen to my question and make sure you understand my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is: Is it fair to say, according to this declaration, the total number of PPU shell casings that are post-1992, that is, the ones that you decided to take into account here, is 378?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I stand corrected, Your Honour. I didn't grasp your question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's 545 less 109, 38, and 20.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In other words, 299 plus 79 is 378?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that is the number that you were interested in, that you were tasked to look for. Post-1992 PPU, 378?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And any -- you know, any casings that related to the period. And that's why we noted the 10 94, and the 324 94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you so much, except that we don't know where they come from, those, the 10 94 and the 324, we don't know which factory they come from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question that I then had was using the figure 3.638, in recognising what you said to His Honour with regard to the 378 casings that have been identified for the years 1993 and 1994 as coming from the PPU, that figure, 378, represents 10.4 per cent of the total number of shell casings that are involved in your declaration; correct?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, I guess you have no questions arising from the questions of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before I do so, before I ask you that question, just one question from the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only one question to ask to be quite sure about the figures you have given. Among the casings you have examined which had no markings, did these casings or cartridges which had no specific mark or were they too damaged so that you couldn't see any specific markings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Most of the shell casings that we examined had markings of some -- the older they were, the more difficult they were to examine. And if we could not readily note that they were from the 1993 to 1995 period, we counted them, but we set them aside and they weren't included in the 1993 to 1994 portions. There was a few shells that we couldn't -- because of rust and contamination, we couldn't tell what factory or what type of markings, but those were rare to find. The other markings were somewhat visible, using the magnifying-glass, to determine the year. If it was pre-1993, we didn't waste much time and we set it aside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No questions, sir, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Selsky. That brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. We want to thank you for coming in to testify. You are now excused. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would this be a convenient time to take a break? We'll take a break and come back at half past. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we could start with revisiting the decision that we withdrew this morning, the oral decision. It's supposed to be in open session. We are in open session. I just have to re-read it all over again, because we withdrew it in its entirety this morning. On the 18th of January, 2010, the Prosecution filed its second Prosecution filing pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision of the 21st of December, 2009, regarding the outstanding documents marked for identification, whereby the Prosecution requests the admission into evidence of six documents, P1279, P1371, P1809, P2149, P2150, and P2151, previously marked for identification. The decision of the 21st December, 2009, denied the admission into evidence of these documents, without prejudice, until such time as a number of conditions set out therein were met. The Prosecution now submits that such conditions have been complied with. And the question to the Defence was: Has the Defence any objection to the admission of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the answer is, no, with the understanding that the Prosecution has complied with the Court's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. And the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the conditions it set out in its decision of the 21st of December, 2009, have been met; admits the mentioned documents into evidence, and orders the following: 1. In relation to P1279, the corresponding B/C/S and English transcripts shall be attached to this exhibit. 2. In relation to P1371, the revised B/C/S translation shall replace the one currently on e-court. 3. In relation to P1809, the full English translation shall replace the six partial and incomplete ones currently on e-court. 4. In relation to P2149, 2150, and 2151, for each of these three exhibits the Prosecution shall re-upload on e-court the B/C/S document complete with the required missing page so that each shall form one complete item. Okay, thank you so much. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the admission of those six documents into evidence, we rest our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic, I seem to recollect that the Defence indicated that they would be in a position to deliver to the Prosecution their witness lists of the Defence within 48 hours of the Prosecution resting. Today is Monday. Wednesday, they shall be delivered?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to meet our obligations by Wednesday, Your Honour. Can we have enough time granted to us, please, by the end of the day? We just have a problem with technical uploading. But, of course, we are going to stick to the dead-line that you are going to give us. We have a technical problem with uploading documents in e-court, and we are literally working on that day and night. What we would like is to have all documents accessible to the OTP straightaway as soon as we give the list. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic, with the caveat that it is not a dead-line set by the Chamber; it's a self-imposed dead-line by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. If you recall, the original decision was the 15th of December, and then you made a decision in writing, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Harmon would tell us when his case is completed, and then within 48 hours we would have to provide our list and our documents. It has to do with your decision in writing, dated the 8th of December. I may be mistaken. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Point taken. I won't take the matter any further. Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. And then to what date shall we then postpone? Are we starting the Defence case on Thursday or on Wednesday? If we give you the whole day, then we start the Defence case on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have a suggestion, Your Honour. I have been told by Mr. Lukic that there are approximately 60 witnesses and a thousand documents. We obviously need to have time to review those. May I suggest that the Court schedule a conference, either a 65 ter conference or a pre-Defence conference. Shortly after receipt of the documents from the Defence, we will be in a better position to inform the Court a number of things relating specifically to compliance with Rule 65 ter, and give Your Honours some insight into our position. But without that at hand, it's difficult for us, at least, to contribute to a meaningful selection of the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And can we schedule that conference for Thursday? Is it possible to do that? Are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, it -- I understood Mr. Lukic to say that there may be some difficulty in uploading this and he will comply, but I don't know if compliance is Wednesday at 5.00 in the afternoon or 8.00 -- 10.00 in the evening. May I suggest Friday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think probably with all the considerations that will go into this, Mr. Harmon's suggestion is a good one and that we schedule a 65 ter conference for Friday. That will give us the time to make sure that we can do the best we can to get all the things up-loaded, with all the difficulties we have, and it will give the Prosecution time to review our documents and make whatever determinations they deem appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We then come back to court on Friday. And if it is Friday, then that's Friday, the 29th. That's in Courtroom I. That's at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 29th day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
